editorial.headline: Construction Equipment Leasing: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers operator-free leasing of construction and civil-engineering equipment—nationally open to full foreign ownership, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the national position is notably more open: the activity is classified as open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For founders assessing a leasing business across Indonesia, the distinction is decisive. National openness does not override Bali’s separate island-wide restriction on PMA registration for the relevant risk classes.

The activity concerns the rental and operational leasing, without an option to purchase, of machinery and equipment used in construction and civil engineering. It includes the associated equipment supplied without an operator: crane lorries, scaffolding and work platforms are clear examples. The boundary is equally important. This is an equipment-leasing activity, not the provision of machinery with personnel; it also excludes the installation and piling of scaffolding and work platforms. In practical terms, the registered business is supplying the asset itself for the customer’s use.

It is open across every stated business scale: Micro, Small, Medium and Large. That breadth makes the national classification useful for a wide range of equipment-leasing models, from a modest fleet serving local projects to a larger specialist operation. The scope is anchored in construction and civil-engineering machinery and its accessories, so the commercial proposition should remain legible as operator-free equipment rental or operational leasing rather than drifting into services outside that definition.

Bali changes the answer for a PMA applicant. At the Large scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, and Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for all KBLI in those risk classes across the island. The stated block took effect under the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. So the accurate reading is not that foreign ownership is capped in Bali; nationally the ceiling remains 100%, while Bali prevents a PMA registration for this activity altogether. A founder may find a nationally open activity on paper, yet still face a firm location-specific stop in Bali.
